nodes.text: AMS-based Yayoi chronology reference used for dating the start of Early Yayoi in one influential framework.
Target Y-chromosome studies report substantial D1a2a/D-M55-related lineages in modern Japanese male populations.
Updated genomic models complicate a simple dual-structure account of Japanese population history.
Dotaku were central to Yayoi ritual systems and later disappear from use and deposition patterns.
Lead isotope analysis can connect dotaku raw materials to external source regions such as the Korean Peninsula and North China.
The Kiki contain narratives of heavenly descent, land creation, land cession or submission, and agricultural-origin motifs.
Continental ancient DNA studies indicate genetic changes and coastal gene flow relevant to later Korean Peninsula and Japanese archipelago population formation.
One influential AMS radiocarbon-based framework places Early Yayoi beginnings around the 10th century BCE.
D1a2a/D-M55 persists at high frequency in modern Japanese male lineages.
Autosomal ancestry models for most mainland Japanese populations are largely continental-derived but regionally variable and increasingly modeled with more than two components.
The combination of largely continental-derived autosomal ancestry and high D1a2a/D-M55 paternal frequency creates a paternal-lineage asymmetry needing interpretation.
Dotaku ritual flourished in western Japan and then ended in the Late Yayoi period.
Dotaku raw materials were connected to external bronze source networks through lead isotope evidence.
The Kiki contain structures of descent, land creation beginning with Awaji, land cession or submission, and Ogetsuhime agricultural-origin motifs.
Continental background studies show Shandong/Haidai genetic change and northern coastal route gene flow relevant to possible Yayoi-to-Kofun ancestry formation.

nodes.text: One influential long chronology places Early Yayoi beginnings around the 10th century BCE.
Y-chromosome asymmetry can preserve signals of sex-biased social structure, reproductive advantage, or elite effects.
A major ritual discontinuity can be interpreted as a possible sign of social or political reorganization, but not proof of it.
Mythic structures may preserve transformed social memory without functioning as direct historical chronicles.
Continental population movements can provide historical context without establishing a direct causal chain to specific Japanese cultural formations.
Multiple independent anomalies can be examined abductively without claiming that any single line of evidence proves the model.
High D1a2a/D-M55 paternal frequency coexists with largely continental-derived autosomal ancestry in many mainland Japanese population models.
Dotaku discontinuity remains a striking ritual-system change that may not be fully explained by simple continuity language.
Kiki narratives repeatedly organize descent, land transfer, submission, and agricultural origins, inviting structured rather than literal comparison with social integration motifs.
Coastal continental gene-flow evidence complicates simplified, single-event migration narratives.
Paternal-lineage asymmetry may reflect some form of social or reproductive advantage rather than passive survival alone.
Dotaku discontinuity may reflect social reorganization, network disruption, ritual authority transfer, or elite replacement, not only internal ritual transformation.
Kiki mythic structures may be examined as possible transformed ritual-political memory, not literal historical record.
Shandong/Haidai and northern coastal gene-flow evidence may provide historical context for Yayoi-to-Kofun continental ancestry, but not a direct proven cause.
The three anomaly families may be considered together as a cross-domain abductive model of Late Yayoi-to-early Kofun social reorganization.
The paternal-lineage asymmetry may indicate some form of social or reproductive advantage for Jomon-associated paternal lineages.
The end of dotaku ritual may reflect social reorganization or network disruption, not solely internal cultural transformation.
Kiki mythic structures may preserve transformed structures of ritual-political memory related to social integration.

Continental East Asian population dynamics around Shandong/Haidai and northern coastal routes may provide historical context for Yayoi-to-Kofun transformations, without proving a direct Shang-Zhou-to-Yayoi causal chain.

The paternal-lineage asymmetry, dotaku discontinuity, Kiki mythic structures, and continental background can be framed as a single testable abductive hypothesis about Late Yayoi-to-early Kofun social reorganization.
The standard Japanese population-history narrative treats Yayoi agriculturalists as demographically overlaying Jomon hunter-gatherers.

Yayoi populations demographically outweighed Jomon groups
Modern Japanese formed through admixture and demographic replacement

nodes.text: D1a2a/D-M55 persistence is best understood as passive Jomon-associated survival rather than a possible social signal.
component_claims: Social-elite interpretations are usually not foregrounded

nodes.text: Dotaku discontinuity is usually treated as internal ritual transformation or cultural transition.
component_claims: Dotaku ritual ended as part of internal cultural change
The end need not imply external disruption

nodes.text: Kiki mythic material is often treated as literary-theological or royal legitimation tradition rather than usable social-historical memory.
component_claims: Mythic structures are difficult to connect to social process
Royal legitimation is the main interpretive frame

nodes.text: Yayoi formation is sometimes narrated as a migration story without precise specification of East Asian source dynamics or staged coastal movements.
component_claims: The specific source dynamics are often simplified
Political events such as Shang-Zhou are rarely integrated

nodes.text: Autosomal ancestry models do not by themselves explain the social-historical meaning of paternal-lineage asymmetry.
Dotaku ritual discontinuity is archaeologically described but not always integrated with population history or later mythic-political narratives.
Kiki mythic structures are often interpreted within textual or legitimation frames without cross-domain testing against archaeological and genetic anomalies.
Continental source dynamics for Yayoi formation are not always connected to specific ancient DNA findings in public or textbook narratives.
No single target paper is responsible for cross-domain consistency among paternal-lineage asymmetry, dotaku discontinuity, and Kiki mythic structures.
Y-chromosome frequency alone cannot prove conquest, elite dominance, or social advantage.
nodes.why_risky: Frequency asymmetry can arise through drift, founder effects, sampling, demography, or social institutions without conquest.
nodes.suggested_patch: Use 'may indicate' and explicitly list alternative explanations and ancient-DNA falsifiers.

nodes.text: Dotaku discontinuity alone cannot prove external disruption or political takeover.
nodes.why_risky: Internal ritual transformation may explain the discontinuity without external social disruption.
nodes.suggested_patch: Frame disruption as one possible interpretation requiring independent support.

nodes.text: Kiki mythic structures cannot be read as literal historical record.
nodes.why_risky: Mythic correspondences can be overread without independent controls.
nodes.suggested_patch: Use method language: possible transformed memory structure, not direct evidence.

nodes.text: A direct Shang-Zhou-to-Yayoi migration chain is not established.
nodes.why_risky: Ancient DNA can indicate regional dynamics and gene flow without proving a specific political-event cause.
nodes.suggested_patch: Use 'historical context' rather than 'direct cause' or 'trigger'.

nodes.text: Calling the Dotaku cultural sphere 'immigrant' overstates the identification of cultural sphere and migrant population.
nodes.why_risky: Dotaku cultural affiliation is not identical to direct immigrant status.
nodes.suggested_patch: Use 'continental-associated Dotaku cultural sphere' or 'Yayoi/Dotaku cultural sphere'.

nodes.text: Combining genetics, archaeology, and myth can create a false impression of proof if the abductive status is not maintained.
nodes.why_risky: Consilience can suggest an explanatory frame but cannot replace domain-specific evidence.
nodes.suggested_patch: State that the model is a working hypothesis and preserve A/B/C/X distinctions.

nodes.text: Representative Kofun elite burials do not show elevated D1a2a/D-M55 compared with non-elite or contemporaneous populations.
nodes.required_evidence: Representative ancient DNA from elite and non-elite Kofun burials.

nodes.text: Regional dotaku chronologies fully explain the discontinuity as continuous local ritual transformation without social network disruption.
nodes.required_evidence: Fine-grained regional archaeological sequences showing continuity without network break or authority transfer.

nodes.text: Kiki descent, land-transfer, and agricultural-origin motifs are shown to be late literary constructions with no stable earlier transmission pattern.
nodes.required_evidence: Textual-historical evidence for late invention or instability of the relevant motifs.

nodes.text: Yayoi-related migration is adequately explained by source dynamics independent of Shandong/Haidai or northern coastal-route ancestry.
nodes.required_evidence: Ancient DNA models excluding Shandong/Haidai-related coastal contribution from relevant Yayoi-to-Kofun transformations.

nodes.text: Neutral demographic models adequately explain modern Y-D1a2a/D-M55 frequency without any sex-biased social advantage.
nodes.required_evidence: Robust population-genetic modeling explaining the paternal/autosomal asymmetry through drift, founder effects, or sampling alone.

nodes.text: The model proposes a candidate explanation across multiple observations; it does not prove the hypothesis.
A/B/C/X/M separates evidence, plausible inference, speculation, overclaim, and method.
Independent lines of evidence may converge on a shared explanatory frame without any single line proving it.

nodes.method_name: Myth as Social Memory, Not Literal Chronicle
nodes.text: Myths are not direct historical records; persistent structures may be examined for possible correspondences under strict caution.
Examples such as Kumulipo show how oral cosmological genealogies can bind creation, descent, ecology, and political legitimacy without being literal chronicles.
Comparative history cases such as Dorian, Germanic, Mongol, Andean, or highland/lowland examples are possibility structures, not evidence for the Japanese case.
Each major claim should state what evidence would weaken or falsify it.
